paper_metadata.title: Quantum generative modeling for financial time series with temporal correlations

summary: The paper studies a Wasserstein QGAN for S&P 500 time-series generation using a hardware-efficient PQC generator and a classical CNN discriminator. It reports a 10-qubit, 8-layer full-state simulation, a 10-qubit, 18-layer MPS simulation with bond dimension 32, and a 20-qubit, 7-layer MPS simulation with bond dimension 70; all are classical simulations, with no quantum hardware or demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Wasserstein QGAN with a hardware-efficient parameterized quantum circuit generator and classical CNN discriminator for synthetic S&P 500 time-series generation, evaluated with full-state simulation.

algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Pauli rotations, nearest-neighbor CNOTs, and data-uploading gates; final variational single-qubit Pauli rotations
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 7900 epochs; best of 5 runs reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: trainable parameters initialized not specified; classical noise input sampled uniformly in [0,2π]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: each qubit contributes two expectation values, <X> and <Z>, post-processed into a time-series sample; classical noise vector uploaded via rotation gates
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize Wasserstein distance between real and generated time-series distributions via critic loss; generator maximizes critic output
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: gradient penalty regularization in Wasserstein GAN critic

problem_instance.description: Generate synthetic financial time series matching S&P 500 log-return distribution and temporal correlations

dataset_specification.description: daily closing prices from 03.01.1950 to 29.9.2021; window length 20; stride 5

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: log returns; normalization to zero mean/unit variance; inverse Lambert-W transform with delta=0.5; renormalization; clipping 0.05% tails; rescaling to [-1,1]; rolling window of length 20
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 5 independent runs; 1500 generated samples for final metric plots; best run reported; confidence intervals as in Chatfield

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: S&P 500 log returns normalized, inverse Lambert-W transformed, clipped, rescaled, rolling-windowed
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: inverse rescaling, renormalization, forward Lambert transform, final renormalization

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical quantum speedup is claimed; the paper reports qualitative performance of a simulator-based QGAN.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware advantage demonstrated; only full-state simulation on a classical computer with 10 qubits and 8 layers.
limiting_factors: Performance compared qualitatively against classical GANs, not a quantum advantage benchmark

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper reports full-state simulation in TensorFlow and no real QPU.
